text:
Maya (oncall): heads up - apiserver watch fanout spiking in eu-west1, started ~12:04 UTC. lots of requeues and slow watch responses.
Ravi: seeing the same, controller-manager leader keeps flipping, affects gpu attach controller.
sre-bot: Incident detected: apiserver_watch_queue_depth > 5000 in eu-west1 (alerting).
Jon: any recent rollout? network team changed proxy timeout yesterday for nat gateway. could be related.
Maya (oncall): no deploys on controlplane, only a couple of training job label changes that create many selectors. suspect hotkey / watch storm from k8s jobs.
Ava: observed huge increase in etcd txn latency around the same time, qps to etcd up 3x. logs show kv txn stalls.
Priya: sample logs:
```
E01 12:04:13.123 apiserver watch handler: enqueue watch (depth=6921)
W01 12:04:13.456 etcdserver: request took too long (ranged reply) tx=0x7f3d err=deadline exceeded
```
Ravi: is this causing GPU provisioning to stall? we have pending attachments in eu-west1-gpu-pool, nodes not attaching.
Maya (oncall): yes, controller-manager reconciliation delayed ~30-120s, attach requests pile up -> kubelet attaches delayed -> scheduler defers new pods -> customers see slow startup and we bill burst capacity.
Jon: quick mitigation ideas: 1) throttle watch resyncs on training-job controllers, 2) increase apiserver watch worker threads, 3) route some requests to read-replica apiservers, 4) fall back to cached responses for attach status.
Ava: short term, can we flip controller-manager leader election lease to longer TTL so it doesn't churn? current setting is 15s. bump to 45s might reduce leader flips while we debug.
Priya: cost tradeoff: increasing watch threads or lease TTL reduces CPU pressure but may temporarily increase token consumption and billed GPU time as VMs stay attached longer. need approval from infra-cost.
Ravi: I'll open a quick config canary for controller-manager TTL and throttling policy on a small controlplane subset. tagging @infra-cost for cost heads-up.
Maya (oncall): deploying canary now to eu-west1-b (10% controlplane nodes). will monitor watch queue and etcd latency.
sre-bot: Canary started: ctrlmgr-ttl-canary -> 10% nodes (eu-west1-b).
Jon: also recommend adding a short-term prefix filter for watchers created by training jobs: collapse identical selectors to single watch where possible. that should cut fanout.
Priya: noted. will prioritize selector dedupe next sprint. for now, if canary looks good, let's keep TTL bump and add a guardrail that limits new watches per namespace to 50.
Maya (oncall): monitoring: watch depth dropped from 7200 -> 680 after canary, etcd p99 down from 1.4s -> 0.9s. continuing to watch for GPU attach backlog.
Ravi: attach backlog trending down 12 -> 3 in eu-west1. good signal.
Ava: keeping an eye on cost impact, but this seems preferable to repeated leader flips and customer outage. add postmortem with action items: selector dedupe, watch rate-limiter, longer lease TTL during peak.
Maya (oncall): thanks all. I'll update the incident ticket and schedule a short follow-up at 13:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
